analysis.title: The Flow Show: Enter the Dragon
key_insights: Year-to-date total returns: oil +72.7%, US stocks +11.9%, global stocks +8.7%, US dollar +3.4%, cash +3.0%, HY bonds -0.9%, IG -2.2%, government bonds -3.0%, gold -6.9%, bitcoin -7.1%.

China is the biggest picture. CSI 300 is down 20% since June, led by tech (-41%), while yields sit at a record low 1.6% and the currency is at a 4-year high against the dollar. BofA reads this as a deflation combination with a consumer and investor buyer strike as property investment keeps falling.
BofA flags China export deflation as the global EPS risk. China exports are up 36% YoY and high-tech exports are up 63% YoY, with monthly high-tech exports at $147bn in Sep'26.

Tale of the tape: US mid caps (MDY above $666), small caps (IJR above $137), global financials (IXG above $125) and NDX holding 28k say the macro backdrop is fine and October risk-off is a tech de-rating in a tightening cycle. Growth 'tells' are breaking down, with MAGS below $70 and TSM below $400, tech EPS revisions falling, and investors the most overweight tech since Aug'20 in the BofA Oct FMS. BRK is at new all-time highs, consistent with a value over growth rotation.

Contrarian long-run call: US Treasury long-run returns in 2026 are the worst in the past 100 years. BofA cites negative long-run returns as good entry points for stocks in 1939, 1974 and 2009 and for commodities in 1933 and 2018, and says a secular contrarian would add bonds. BofA adds to 'peak yield' plays: small cap, REITs, utilities and consumer discretionary.
Weekly flows: $55.6bn to stocks, $28.8bn to cash, $12.1bn to bonds, $2.6bn to gold and $0.2bn to crypto. Stock flows were $67.3bn into ETFs and $11.7bn out of mutual funds.

Notable flows: Treasuries $5.4bn in (17th straight week), Japan equities $6.0bn in (largest since Apr'26), China equities $17.0bn in (largest since Jul'26), Korea equities $5.8bn in (largest since Jul'26), tech $18.8bn in (largest since Jul'26), energy $1.1bn in (largest since Apr'26).

Capitulation-style outflows: consumer funds lost $2.1bn (largest since Feb'14, 2nd largest ever) and utilities lost $1.6bn (largest since Mar'15, 2nd largest ever). BofA treats these as support for its 'peak yield' adds in utilities and consumer discretionary.

By region and style: EM equities have 4 weeks of inflows ($33.5bn), US 3 weeks ($6.7bn), Japan 2 weeks ($6.0bn), while Europe has 2 weeks of outflows ($1.0bn). US small cap lost $7.5bn and US growth lost $2.6bn, while US large cap gained $4.5bn and US value $1.9bn.

BofA Bull & Bear Indicator fell to 7.2 from 7.4 on weak global stock index breadth, bearish hedge fund positioning in oil and S&P 500 futures and wider junk bond spreads, partly offset by strong equity inflows. The signal is neutral after 'extreme bull' readings all summer. The 'old' indicator rose to 5.3 from 5.1.

BofA Breadth Rule: net 30% of global equity indices are oversold (below both 50-day and 200-day averages). The contrarian buy signal needs net 88%, which would take US, Taiwan and Brazil equity indices falling 5-10% from current levels.

BofA's view is tactically risk-off until mid-Nov. It expects yields down (GT30 toward 5%), stocks down and the US dollar down (DXY below 100) until the midterm Democratic sweep is fully priced, the ECB or French government stops the rout in French bonds, or an AI capex cut or extreme equity issuance announcement peaks AI hyperscaler debt spreads.
A Democratic sweep is read as negative for EPS because it ends the lower tax and regulation regime and leaves Trump less able to push resources and capital into the US-China AI priority.

Near-term upside risk is a US announcement of Russia, Ukraine or Iran peace deals that collapse oil by $10-20/bbl. Near-term downside risk is hyperscaler bond spreads surging above 200bps, with investors deleveraging on shadow banking credit event risk.

Three 2027 scenarios: AI bubble, Goldilocks broadening, and deflationary bust. The bubble case rests on the AI = railroads analogy, an unprecedented US government backstop of AI and a structural buy-the-dip habit among Gen Z and Gen X. The breadth case rests on consensus expecting a 40bps drop in UST yields and 15% SPX EPS growth in '27, with small and mid caps on 15x PE. The bust case rests on railroads having three 30-50% drawdowns in their late-1800s bull and on credit tightening cutting the $1.2tn AI hyperscaler '27 capex forecast.

BofA thinks consensus conviction in the bubble scenario (50% of Oct FMS respondents predicted 'no landing') and the breadth scenario (40% 'soft landing') are both too high. Fear of a 'hard landing' bust (6%) is too low. The next big entry point for risk assets comes when policy makers are forced to ease financial conditions and fear is more visible.

Without an AI boom there is no boom, unless oil falls $30/bbl, yields fall 100-150bps or China stimulates. That risks downward revisions to '27 forecasts of 5% US nominal GDP and 43% global tech EPS growth, after 92% in '26.

Event calendar: Brazil election Oct 25, Israel election Oct 27, FOMC and UK budget plus MSFT and GOOG earnings Oct 28, ECB Oct 29, BoJ Oct 30, US ISM Nov 2, US midterms Nov 3 and the APEC summit in Shenzhen Nov 18 (Xi, Trump and Putin all attending).

BofA private clients hold $4.6tn AUM at 65.9% stocks, 17.4% bonds and 9.4% cash. Over four weeks they bought municipal bond, industrials and healthcare ETFs and sold staples, EM debt and consumer discretionary ETFs. Equity ETF share count rose 0.3% in the week and is up 8.3% YTD.

Proprietary rules: FMS Cash Indicator at 3.9% gives a Sell signal, the EM Flow Trading Rule at 1.9% gives a Sell, the Global Flow Trading Rule at 0.2% is neutral, and the Global EPS Growth Model at 35% signals EPS growth rising over 6-12 months.

tension_points.bull_case: AI follows the railroad analogy, the US government is backstopping AI, Gen Z and Gen X buy dips, and consensus expects a 40bps fall in UST yields and 15% SPX EPS growth in 2027, which could broaden the rally to small and mid caps on 15x PE.
tension_points.bear_case: Railroads had three 30-50% drawdowns in their late-1800s bull, bonds end booms, and credit tightening could cut the $1.2tn AI hyperscaler 2027 capex forecast, leading to downward revisions to 5% US nominal GDP and 43% global tech EPS growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler bond spreads surging above 200bps, or an AI capex cut or extreme equity issuance announcement, would break the bull case.
